transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-10 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Lumenix Head of ML), Samir Patel (Lumenix Platform Eng), Maya Chen (Lumenix Security)

Summary (auto): Align technical and ops steps for Dedicated pilot and go-live readiness.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, um this is Alex from Redwood, with Priya our SE. Quick intros?
[00:12] Jordan (Lumenix): Jordan here, Head of ML at Lumenix, we run the recommendation and search stacks.
[00:16] Samir: Samir, infra, I manage clusters and networking.
[00:19] Maya: Maya, security and compliance.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Great—I'll be driving the runbook and the benchmarks.
[00:27] Alex: Goal for today, surface any blockers for the Dedicated pilot, talk about SSO, VPC peering, data retention, SLA targets, and agree next steps.

[02:03] Jordan: Quick context—we want to move our personalization service off a fragile internal endpoint onto Redwood, aim for p95 latency under 180ms and costs under $X per 1k requests. Pilot window two weeks.

[03:15] Priya: Sounds good. For Dedicated, we can reserve a GPU pool, and there's burst capacity. We'll need to size based on token distribution and concurrency. Do you have typical request sizes?
[03:29] Samir: Mostly short prompts, average 120 tokens in and 40 out, spikes during promo windows. Throughput target around 200 rps during peak.

[04:45] Priya: Okay that maps to N GPUs for baseline—I'll put numbers in the sizing doc. Also we recommend enabling KV cache for prefix reuse to reduce per-token cost, sorry K-V cash in some transcripts...

[06:10] Maya: From security side, we need SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration. Also audit logs retention for 12 months.

[07:02] Alex: We support SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC in the Console, and customer-managed KMS in Private/ Dedicated. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 report.

[08:44] Jordan: About data residency—some PII must stay in EU region, is that possible with Dedicated?
[08:55] Priya: Yes for Dedicated we can pin region; for Private on-prem we'd give full control. For hosted we have region constraints. We'll document the region pinning flow.

[10:20] Samir: Network question—how does VPC peering work? We want minimal NAT or public egress.
[10:31] Priya: We offer VPC peering and private link options; for Dedicated we can do VPC peering into our serving subnets and route traffic over private paths. There may be firewall rules to open. We'll send a network diagram.

[12:02] Maya: Also curious about logs—do we store request payloads? We need to control retention and PII redaction.
[12:14] Alex: By default we retain minimal telemetry; payload retention is configurable. We can set retention windows and optionally enable automatic PII redaction or have you redact before sending. We'll detail options in the security doc.

[14:00] Jordan: Success criteria: p95 under 180ms, uptime 99.9, cost under the X benchmark. If we hit those in pilot we go to production.

[15:45] Priya: For benchmarks we'll run a supervised run with your sample payloads and our load driver, collect latency histograms and token cost. Need your sample traces and payloads.

[17:10] Samir: We'll share traces and a synthetic workload by Monday. Also want the runbook: escalation, contact lists, code samples for SDK.

[19:00] Priya: Runbook will include oncall escalation, fallback to hosted variant, rollback steps, and cache invalidation. We'll build a draft before the workshop.

[21:30] Alex: On commercials—pilot pricing can be usage-based with a short-term commit for Dedicated. We can put together the pilot SOW. Any procurement constraints?

[22:05] Jordan: Legal needs standard NDA + security addendum, procurement may require PO under $Y threshold.

[23:15] Maya: Also need the mapping for SAML attributes and SCIM provisioning for user access.

[24:10] Priya: We'll attach a sample SAML metadata and SCIM schema.

[26:00] Jordan: One more thing—what about model version pinning and rollouts? We don't want surprise regen changes.

[26:12] Priya: You can pin a model version per route and do canary rollouts. The Console shows per-route metrics and rollouts. Note sometimes transcripts call it "Redwood controls" but it's Redwood Console.

[28:55] Samir: If we do on-prem later, what's involved?
[29:04] Alex: Private deploy is more involved—packaging, K8s configs, airgap options, HSM integration. We can scope that if the pilot succeeds.

[31:30] Maya: For KMS—support for customer-managed keys? We need AES-GCM and rotation policy.

[31:48] Alex: Yes, customer KMS/HSM is supported in Private and Dedicated with some caveats. We'll include supported KMS vendors in the security packet.

[34:02] Priya: Operationally, we recommend a canary rollout for the first week, then ramp if metrics look good. We'll instrument endpoints with tracing headers so you can correlate requests.

[36:15] Jordan: Ok timeline—if we get pricing and SOW this week, we can kick pilot next Monday and run two-week window.

[37:20] Alex: Great. Let's enumerate next steps: we'll share pricing, security docs, network diagram, and schedule the runbook workshop.

[38:55] Samir: Small nit—how are SDKs versioned? We have a Node and Python stack.

[39:12] Priya: SDKs published on npm and pip with semver, and we provide sample integrations. We'll send code snippets for streaming and function calling.

[41:00] Maya: Anything about audit logs format? We need JSON structured logs for SIEM ingest.

[41:22] Alex: We output structured JSON audit logs and support forwarding to your logging endpoint or pushing to S3 with lifecycle rules.

[43:30] Jordan: Can you run a smoke test with our staging keys before we start pilot?

[43:45] Priya: Yes, we can provision staging credentials; need the SCIM user list so we can give access.

[45:05] Alex: Alright, unless there are more big blockers—
[45:12] Maya: One more—do you support PCI-type redaction for card numbers in transcripts?

[45:26] Priya: We have regex-based redaction and also advise not to send raw card numbers. We'll document recommended practices.

[46:40] Jordan: Sounds good.

[48:00] Alex: Recap and owners: Alex will send pricing and SOW; Priya will schedule runbook workshop and draft benchmarks; Samir will send traces/payloads; Maya will finish security questionnaire. We'll target to have all artifacts by next Wednesday.

[50:12] Jordan: Thanks all.

[50:20] Maya: Thanks.

[50:27] Priya: Thanks; we'll follow up with calendar invites.

End of transcript.
